cards.explanation: The answer is pure joy, friends. James says, “Consider it pure joy, my brothers, when you encounter trials of many kinds…” (James 1:2). He doesn't say a little joy or a sprinkle of joy. He says PURE. I'd have bet money he'd say "grit your teeth," so he got me too.

The answer is perseverance, friends. James says the testing of your faith develops it (James 1:3). So the trial isn't just something to survive. It's building something in you. And in the next verse he tells his brothers to let that work finish.

The answer is mature and complete, friends. James says to allow perseverance to finish its work “…so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.” (James 1:4). That's a full batch, golden all the way through. He's not talking about a half-finished thing.

The answer is God, friends. James says, “Now if any of you lacks wisdom, he should ask God…” (James 1:5). He points the one who lacks wisdom straight to God. And he adds right away that God gives generously.

The answer is True. James says God “…gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to him.” (James 1:5). Generously, to ALL, with no fault-finding. So you can walk up and ask without rehearsing an apology first.

The answer is a wave tossed by the wind, friends. James says the one who doubts “…is like a wave of the sea, blown and tossed by the wind.” (James 1:6). One minute up, one minute down, going wherever the wind pushes. That's a picture you can see in your head right away.

The answer is False, and James is plain about it. He says, “That man should not expect to receive anything from the Lord.” (James 1:7). The man he means is the one who asks while doubting. In the verse before, James says that doubter is like a wave of the sea (James 1:6).

The answer is low, friends. James says the humble brother should exult in his high position, “But the one who is rich should exult in his low position…” (James 1:9-10). It's a switch. The humble one looks up, and the rich one gets pointed down.

The answer is because he will pass away, friends. James says the rich man “…will pass away like a flower of the field.” (James 1:10). Then he describes the sun rising with scorching heat and withering the plant. His point is that the rich man will fade, in the midst of his pursuits (James 1:11).

The answer is True. James says the man who perseveres under trial “…will receive the crown of life that God has promised to those who love Him.” (James 1:12). That's God's promise, not James's guess. And it comes after the man has stood the test.

The answer is False, friends. James says no one should say “God is tempting me.” His reason is that “…God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does He tempt anyone.” (James 1:13). Nobody gets to pass the blame upstairs.

The answer is his own evil desires, friends. James says, “But each one is tempted when by his own evil desires he is lured away and enticed.” (James 1:14). Each one means each one, so nobody gets a pass. It's his own desires doing the luring.

The answer is that it gives birth to death, friends. James says, “Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.” (James 1:15). He lays out the chain step by step: desire, sin, then death. It's a heavy verse.

The answer is above, friends. James says, “Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights…” (James 1:17). God tempts no one, and He gives every good and perfect gift. That's a good one to remember when you're feeling pulled around.

The answer is the word of truth, friends. James says, “He chose to give us birth through the word of truth…” (James 1:18). The Father chose it and did it that way. And I love the word chose, since I know what it's like to be picked.
